summary: In this excerpt from Book 4, a young woman named Valentine is confronted in a foreign city by a soldier who is clearly reluctant to harm her. Neither can understand the other's language, so they communicate through a few borrowed phrases from movies. Valentine calms him by sharing butter-balls with him, then introduces herself, learns his name is Withnail, and asks him to let her go to save her family. The passage ends with her reflecting on her mortality and on her need to return to her own trenches.
one_line: Valentine, a young woman in wartime, wins over a reluctant enemy soldier named Withnail by sharing butter-balls and asking to be released.
key_facts: Valentine knows a few words of the foreign language, learned from a cinema across from her block of flats.
The soldier speaks a different language she does not recognize, then switches to Hindi.
Valentine's only Hindi phrase is 'Love Love Love I'm in Love', the chorus of Hindi movie songs.
The soldier's handgun is described as a soft, floppy weapon like a length of rope.
Valentine reasons that the soldier does not want to kill her and is angry because he will have to.
Valentine reaches into her pocket for butter-balls, and she and the soldier eat them together, bite by bite.
Valentine thinks that if she were a suicide bomber, the soldier would already be dead, which makes her feel better about the war.
The soldier introduces himself as Withnail.
Valentine says 'Pleased to make your acquaintance, Withnail' in his language, though she suspects she pronounces it wrongly.
Valentine tells Withnail, 'To save my family,' and says she is on a mission for his side anyway.
Withnail slowly releases her arm after she squeezes his hand and asks him to let her go.
Valentine has never kissed a boy and expects to be dead in four days and a little more.
Valentine fears she may die that afternoon if she cannot get back into her own trenches.

entities.name: Withnail
entities.role: soldier from the other side who holds Valentine at gunpoint and later lets her go
